subtopics.title: The Laws — and Why They Are True

questions.question: x⁴ × x² simplifies to:
options: x⁶ — same base multiplied, add the exponents

questions.question: Why does anything nonzero to the power zero equal one?
options: Because zero times anything is zero
Because x⁴/x⁴ is both 1 (a thing divided by itself) and x⁰ (by the subtraction law) — two names for one value

questions.question: A negative exponent, such as x⁻³, means:
options: The reciprocal — 1/x³; it is an address, not a sign
x³ with the answer made negative

questions.question: (3x)² equals:
options: 9x² — every factor inside the bracket takes the power

questions.question: (3xy²)² expands to:
options: 9x²y⁴ — square the 3, square the x, and double y's counter to 4

questions.question: Gathering 9x²y⁴ × 2x⁻³ gives:
In the final division, y⁴ over y⁴ disappears because:
options: y is assumed to be zero

questions.question: The polished final answer for the whole expression is:
options: 3/x² — the negative exponent is moved downstairs for the final form

subtopics.title: Solving Three to the x Plus One Equals Twenty-Seven

questions.question: The central move for solving 3^(x+1) = 27 is:
options: Writing both sides as powers of the same base: 3^(x+1) = 3³
Taking the square root of both sides
Multiplying the base by the exponent

questions.question: Why may the exponents be equated once the bases match?
options: Because equal powers of the same positive base (not 1) can only come from equal exponents
It is an approximation that usually works

questions.question: If the right side were 1/9 instead of 27, the equation 3^(x+1) = 1/9 gives:
'Dividing both sides by 3 to peel off the exponent' is wrong because:
options: Division is never allowed in equations
Dividing by 3 only lowers the exponent by one — it does not free the exponent, and writing x + 1 = 9 breaks the mathematics

subtopics.title: The Error Museum — and the Full Method

questions.question: Writing (3xy²)² as 3x²y⁴ commits which museum error?
options: The coefficient dodged the bracket's power — the 3 must become 9
Multiplying the base by the exponent

questions.question: x² × y³ does NOT equal xy⁵ because:
options: The exponents should be multiplied instead
The laws compress only powers of the SAME base — x's and y's live in separate piles

questions.question: 2x⁻³ written correctly with a positive exponent is:
options: 2/x³ — only the x³ moves downstairs; the 2 stays where it is

questions.question: The absurdity that convicts 'multiply the base by the exponent' is:

subtopics.title: Exponents Just Count How Many Times

questions.question: In the counting picture, x⁴ × x² = x⁶ because:
options: Four x's and two x's pushed together make one pile of six
Six is the biggest allowed exponent

questions.question: x² divided by x⁵ leaves 1/x³ because:
options: Two cancel above and three remain standing below — which is also x⁻³ by the subtracting rule

questions.question: The minus in a negative exponent is best read as:
options: A sign that makes the value negative
An address — it sends the power to the other side of the fraction line

subtopics.title: Everyone in the Taxi Pays the Fare

questions.question: The taxi-fare rule for (3xy²)² says:
options: Only the letters pay the fare
Every passenger inside the bracket — the 3, the x, and the y² — gets squared; nobody rides free
The fare is optional for coefficients

questions.question: 'Sorting the washing' during simplification means:
options: Working numbers with numbers, x's with x's, y's with y's — separate piles, one law per line

questions.question: The quick number check at x = 1, y = 1 gave 3 for the original and 3 for the answer. This shows:
options: The identity is fully proven for all x and y
The simplification survives its first test — one substitution catches nearly every slip cheaply

subtopics.title: Speak Both Sides in the Same Language

questions.question: 'Translating' 27 in the equation 3^(x+1) = 27 means:
options: Rewriting 27 as 3³ so both sides speak powers of three
Swapping the sides of the equation

questions.question: Solving 2^(x+1) = 32 by the same move gives:
If the right side is 1, the translation is:
options: 1 cannot be written as a power of 3
1 = 3⁰, so the whole exponent equals zero

questions.question: Rewriting 3^(x+1) as 3(x + 1) is forbidden because:
options: The bracket is in the wrong place
It only works for even exponents
The 3 should be on the right side
The counter counts multiplications of 3 by itself — it never multiplies the 3; otherwise 3³ would be 9, not 27
